English keeps the meaning but is written as English, and drops claims the product cannot back (100 %, best, guarantee) — the same line V29 took for `v29.why`.

marketing:v11.hero.title.en: Studying in Korea is easier than you think

marketing:v11.hero.lede.en:
Find the right Korean university and get every step done, with a team beside you.
Start with what you want to study.

marketing:v11.why.title.en:
With Hangyul,
studying abroad gets simpler

marketing:v11.why.s2.text.en: Every student starts from a different place. We build your plan from your grades, your goals and your budget, so the universities we suggest are ones you can realistically reach.

marketing:v29.why.s1.title.en:
As much help as you need,
start to finish

marketing:v29.why.s1.text.en: Universities, documents, visa, arrival: you choose the stages you want help with. Each plan says exactly what we do, so you know what you get before you start.

marketing:v29.why.s3.text.en: You see the scope before you pay, and you pay once, in US dollars. We don't promise admission; we make your preparation clear and on time.

marketing:v11.services.title.en:
From your first question
to your first weeks in Korea

marketing:v11.services.lede.en:
One team helps you from planning your application
until you have settled in.

marketing:v11.services.s1.title.en: Universities and language institutes chosen for you

marketing:v11.services.s1.text.en: We suggest universities and Korean language institutes that fit your record and your goals. In a one-to-one consultation we also go through the scholarships you can apply for, then help you prepare your documents and deal with the university.
marketing:v11.services.s1.text.why: 'take care of the whole process' over-promised; 'communicating with the university' stiff

marketing:v11.services.s2.title.en: After your offer: help until you have settled in

marketing:v11.services.s2.text.en: We help you through your visa application, your residence card and course registration, the steps that come after you are admitted, so you can start your studies on a steady footing.

marketing:v11.services.s3.title.en: A community of students who have been there

marketing:v11.services.s3.text.en: Meet other admitted students to swap tips on housing and daily life, and build your network before you arrive.

marketing:v11.faq.q1.q.en: Which documents do I need to apply?

marketing:v11.faq.q2.q.en: Do I need a TOPIK score?

marketing:v11.faq.q2.a.en: Most Korean universities ask for a Korean or English test result (TOPIK, TOEFL or IELTS). Some also accept their own Korean-language test instead.

marketing:v11.faq.q3.a.en: Universities accept TOPIK, TOEFL and IELTS. Some also accept a certificate from a university's Korean language institute in Korea, a pass in the university's own Korean test, or a King Sejong Institute certificate at intermediate level 1 or above.

marketing:v11.faq.q4.q.en: Can I apply if I don't speak Korean?

marketing:v11.faq.q4.a.en: Yes. On an English-taught programme you can study entirely in English.

marketing:v11.faq.q5.a.en: They depend on the university and the programme. We recommend starting at least six months before your course begins so there is time to prepare your documents. Language courses usually need less lead time.
marketing:v11.faq.q5.a.why: 'So that preparing your documents is comfortable'

marketing:v11.faq.q6.q.en: Which universities offer scholarships to international students?

marketing:v11.faq.q6.a.en: Most do, but the amounts and the conditions differ from one university to another.

marketing:v11.faq.q7.a.en: There is no minimum grade to apply to a Korean university, but higher grades give you a better chance at the universities you want.

marketing:v11.faq.q8.a.en: Most Korean universities have no age limit, though a few do. If that applies to you, we can suggest universities where age is not an issue. Either way you need a high-school or junior-college graduation certificate.

marketing:v11.faq.q9.q.en: Can I start university straight after high school?

marketing:v11.faq.q9.a.en: Yes. You can apply to a Korean university as soon as you graduate from high school or junior college.

marketing:v11.faq.q10.q.en: Is it easy to find a job in Korea after graduating?

marketing:v11.faq.q10.a.en: It depends on your field. Graduates in engineering and business usually find work more easily than graduates in the humanities.

marketing:v11.cta.title.en: Start your Korean study plan today

marketing:v11.cta.text.en: Create a free account to see the programmes you can apply to and the documents you will need, based on your own profile.
marketing:v11.cta.text.why: shorter; 'free' — account creation has no charge (true: plans are bought separately)
